description: Variant-aware ModelSelect with inline variant chips: extend the shared UI primitive, add a variant data-access hook, and migrate the issue-detail, settings, and create-issue surfaces to select model + variant in a single control.

tasks.title: Variant-aware ModelSelect primitive with inline chips and keyboard nav
tasks.description: Extend the shared `packages/web/src/shared/ui/ModelSelect.tsx` with optional additive props (`modelVariants`, `valueVariant`, `onChangeVariant`), add a co-located `model-variants.ts` helper module (`variantListFor`, `resolveVariantAgainstModel`), introduce an internal `ModelVariantChips` subcomponent that renders inline on variant-capable rows, and implement a `chipFocus` keyboard state machine (↑↓ rows, → into chips, Enter/Tab/Esc). The `onChange: (model) => void` signature stays unchanged so every existing caller keeps working with zero edits; with no variant props supplied the component renders exactly as today. Include full unit tests.
acceptanceCriteria: ModelSelect renders one chip per variant only on rows whose model id is present in `modelVariants`; rows without variants render no chips and behave as before.

Clicking a variant chip invokes `onChange(modelId)` and `onChangeVariant(variant)` then closes the popover; clicking a model row body invokes `onChange(modelId)` and `onChangeVariant(null)` (default variant) then closes the popover.
The active variant chip within the selected model row is visually filled/highlighted; all other chips on that row render as outline; a selected model with no variant shows no active chip.

Keyboard flow works without leaving the popover: ↑↓ move the highlighted model row, → moves focus into the chip row of a variant-capable highlighted model, Enter selects the focused chip (or the highlighted model with default variant when not in a chip row), Esc closes.
With `size="compact"` chips use the compact size; at a 375px viewport a 4-chip row wraps gracefully and every chip remains a ≥44x44 px tap target including padding.
Search filtering preserves chips on surviving rows.

`packages/web/src/shared/ui/ModelSelect.test.tsx` is extended with cases for: inline chip rendering on variant-capable rows, no chips on non-variant rows, chip-click selection (model+variant+close), model-body click (default variant), active-chip highlight, keyboard navigation into and within the chip row, compact-size rendering, and chip preservation under search.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass, including all pre-existing ModelSelect tests with no variant props supplied.
tasks.notes: Purely additive and backward-compatible. VariantPicker.tsx does not exist in the codebase and must NOT be created — `model-variants.ts` is greenfield. `ModelVariantChips` must be a separately importable subcomponent so the bespoke IssueModelSelector popover can reuse it in T-003 (design decision D2).

tasks.title: Model variants data-access hook
tasks.spec: specs/model-select/spec.md#ModelSelect renders inline variant chips on variant-capable rows
tasks.description: Add a `useModelVariants()` hook in the settings entity layer (`packages/web/src/entities/settings`) that returns `Record<string, string[]>` keyed by model id, sourced from runner model discovery. Until prerequisite #238 exposes variant data it SHALL return `{}` (and the UI renders no chips), so the hook is safe to merge ahead of #238. Include unit tests covering the empty/default path and the populated path using mock data.
acceptanceCriteria: `useModelVariants()` returns a `Record<string, string[]>` and never throws when variant data is unavailable (returns `{}`).
When the underlying discovery data exposes variants for a model, the hook returns that model's variant list keyed by model id.
The hook is exported from the settings entity public API so IssueModelSelector, AiSettingsSection, and CreateIssueDialog can consume it.
Unit tests cover both the empty/default path and a populated path using mocked discovery data.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and the relevant entity-layer tests pass.
tasks.notes: Implementation detail of where variant data arrives (new API field vs separate endpoint) is abstracted inside this hook; it does not change the design if #238 chooses a different transport. The hook has no code dependency on T-001 but is priority-ordered after it.

tasks.title: Variant-aware model selection in Issue detail (default + per-stage)
tasks.spec: specs/web-ui/spec.md#Web UI supports issue model overrides
tasks.description: Migrate `packages/web/src/features/select-issue-model/ui/IssueModelSelector.tsx` to select model + variant through the unified pattern. Its default-model popover is bespoke (it does NOT use the shared ModelSelect), so render the shared `ModelVariantChips` subcomponent inside its `ModelListItem`; its per-stage rows already use shared `ModelSelect`, so pass `modelVariants`, `valueVariant`, and `onChangeVariant` through. Persist the selected variant alongside the model via the existing workflow-variable patch endpoints (`patchIssueWorkflowDefinitionVar` / `patchIssueWorkflowStageDefinitionVar`), reading the current variant from the issue's `modelVariant` / `stageModelVariants`. Include tests.
acceptanceCriteria: The Issue detail default-model popover renders variant chips inline on variant-capable model rows via the shared `ModelVariantChips` subcomponent; no standalone variant dropdown appears next to it.
Selecting a chip on the default model updates the issue's model variant through the issue API and the popover closes; selecting the model body selects the default (no) variant.
Per-stage override rows use the shared `ModelSelect` with `size="compact"` and the inline-chip pattern; selecting a chip updates that stage's model variant.
The currently active variant for the default model and for each stage is read from `modelVariant` / `stageModelVariants` and rendered as the active chip.

Component tests cover: chip rendering in the bespoke default-model popover, chip-click persistence for default and stage models, default-variant selection on body click, and per-stage compact chip rendering.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.notes: Do NOT rewrite the bespoke default-model popover onto the shared ModelSelect — its recent-models/loading/error/fuzzysort features stay (design Non-Goal). Only add chip rendering via the shared subcomponent. Confirm variant persistence field names against the actual issue API during implementation.

tasks.title: Variant-aware model selection in Settings AI defaults and Create Issue dialog
tasks.spec: specs/web-ui/spec.md#Web UI supports issue model overrides
tasks.description: Migrate the two remaining shared-`ModelSelect` surfaces: `packages/web/src/pages/settings/ui/AiSettingsSection.tsx` (project default model + per-stage overrides) and `packages/web/src/features/create-issue/ui/CreateIssueDialog.tsx` (issue-creation model picker). Pass `modelVariants`, `valueVariant`, and `onChangeVariant` to each ModelSelect, persist the variant through the existing stage-model mutation path (Settings) and include the variant in the create-issue request when set (Create Issue). Include tests for both surfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings → AI defaults selector and its per-stage override rows render variant chips inline via the unified ModelSelect and select model + variant in one action.
Create Issue dialog model picker renders variant chips inline and, when a variant is chosen, the create request includes the variant alongside the model.
No standalone variant dropdown appears on either surface.
Component tests cover chip rendering and chip-click selection in AiSettingsSection (default + at least one stage) and in CreateIssueDialog (variant included in the create payload).
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
Stage lists on Settings still include `integrate` and exclude `fix` (unchanged behavior preserved).
tasks.notes: If CreateIssueDialog turns out to use a bespoke control instead of shared ModelSelect (open question Q1 in design.md), apply the same ModelVariantChips subcomponent approach used in T-003 rather than forcing a full rewrite. Both surfaces are bundled because they perform identical shared-ModelSelect wiring, avoiding duplicate near-identical tasks.
